items.note: The Udayeśvara temple is based on a Śaiva sect deriving from Śaiva Siddhānta; built by Udayāditya Paramāra; the Paramāras followed this sect; Bhoja's Tattvaprakāśa is one of its most authentic texts.
Man may aspire to the company of the lord (śivasāyujya); the temple is a standing reminder of this possibility.
Bhoja's Tattvaprakāśa was the most important text for the Northern school of Śaiva Siddhāntins; its two commentaries give it virtually canonical status.
Basic constituents of Śaiva Siddhānta: pati, paśu and pāśa.
Thirty-six tattvas, the last five forming the śuddha addhvā (pure path).
Five pure principles Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara and Vidyā explained as moments of infinite consciousness; background to the śukanāsa interpretation.
